questions.q: Why does `storefront` use two separate GitHub Actions workflows instead of one that watches the whole repo?
options: GitHub Actions does not support monorepos
Path filters let each service's workflow trigger only on changes under its own services/ folder, avoiding wasted rebuilds
Node.js and Python apps cannot share a workflow file under any circumstances
Two workflows run in parallel for no technical reason, purely by convention
questions.explain: Each service's workflow uses a `paths` filter (e.g. `services/checkout/**`) so a change to one service never triggers a rebuild and rescan of the other.

questions.q: In the CI pipeline, what does Trivy scan, and what does it block on?
options: It scans the git diff and blocks on any mention of a password
It scans the built container image and blocks the pipeline on CRITICAL vulnerabilities that already have a fix available
It scans Terraform files and blocks on misconfigured resource groups
It scans Helm chart values and blocks on missing defaults
questions.explain: Trivy is a container image vulnerability scanner. This pipeline configures it to block on CRITICAL findings that have a fix available, rather than failing on every low-severity finding.

questions.q: Why are images pushed to ACR tagged with the git SHA instead of `latest`?
options: ACR does not allow the tag `latest`
SHA tags are shorter and faster to type
A SHA tag makes every image traceable to the exact commit that produced it, which later makes rollback to a known-good image possible
SHA tags are required by Trivy to run a scan
questions.explain: `latest` always points to whatever was pushed most recently, so it can't be used to roll back. A SHA tag is immutable and traceable to one commit.

questions.q: What does gitleaks scan for, and where does it run in this pipeline?
options: It scans the container image for vulnerable OS packages, and runs only in CI
It scans the diff for things that look like committed credentials, and runs both as a local pre-commit hook and as a CI step
It scans Kubernetes manifests for missing resource limits, and runs only at deploy time
It scans the Terraform state file for drift, and runs only on a schedule
questions.explain: gitleaks inspects diffs for secret-shaped strings (API keys, tokens, connection strings). It's wired in twice — a pre-commit hook locally and a CI step — so a secret has two chances to be caught before merge.

options: gitleaks will be replaced by a different scanner in a later phase
A PaymentPro test API key almost got committed directly into a Helm values.yaml file, and gitleaks caught it before it merged

gitleaks found a critical vulnerability in the checkout image
questions.explain: The lesson lightly foreshadows a near-miss secrets leak — a PaymentPro test key almost committed into a Helm values file, caught by gitleaks — with the full worked example reserved for Chapter 5.
